dedupe_keys.name: iberian blackout of april 2025 and the internet core traffic routing and data centre power failure at four ixps acm ccr 2026

description: This case study summarises a peer-reviewed measurement of how the April 2025 Iberian power blackout affected the Internet core. Using traffic profiles at four of the largest exchange points on the peninsula, active probing and global BGP routing data, the authors found that IXP traffic dropped by 33% to 70% within minutes yet settled at overnight levels, not vanishing, showing that backup generators and batteries largely kept core infrastructure running. The study also found a previously unreported second event: hours into the blackout, diesel generators failed at a major data centre, cutting power to part of the building, and the resulting loss of BGP sessions to the IXP route server rippled through routing data worldwide. Amateur radio reports from PSKReporter were used to separate who had power from who had Internet. Producer: Internet Society Pulse blog by Oliver Hohlfeld (University of Kassel) with authors from the University of Kassel and DE-CIX; the paper is in ACM CCR 2026. Coverage: Spain and Portugal, with global routing effects. Access: the blog post was read; the full paper was not opened. Licence and cost: free to read; licence not stated. Caveats: numbers are those quoted in the blog summary, and the data centre is not named. Simulation uses: the traffic drop ranges and the generator failure sequence give calibration for resilience and cascading-failure models of interconnection facilities. Related records: ISOC Pulse IXP power substation dependency simulation (case_study-isoc-pulse-ixp-power-substation-dependency-simulation) and IODA (data-ioda-internet-outage-detection).
